resources.string: Starting dimensions for round and square 27 MHz Halo antennas and a reference for the CSQ‑11.

k = P / (λ / 2), where P is the full perimeter along the conductor centreline, including the gap, and λ is the wavelength. At k = 1 the perimeter is half a wavelength. The default of 1.02 makes it 2% longer.
Measure the gap in a straight line between the centres of the ends.
Enter a frequency from 26 to 28 MHz.
Enter a gap from 1 mm up to one quarter of the diameter or side.
f is in MHz. Dimensions in the formulas are in metres. L is the conductor length along its centreline.

Enter any known dimensions of your gamma match. The gap, shorting strap position and capacitance affect one another. For matching calculations, measure the radiator resistance and reactance in its installed position.
Enter lengths from 0.1 to 3000 mm and capacitance from 0.1 to 1000 pF. Keep the conductors apart and the strap within the length of the rod.

Place the antenna horizontally for horizontal polarization. Tune in the intended installation position. A feed-point choke helps reduce current on the outside of the coax shield. Adjust the gap, then refine the strap position and capacitance using SWR and impedance at the target frequency. Measure again after each adjustment.
Geometry is calculated using formulas from the publications. See the original publications for their terms of use.
Historical 11 m design. A complete cut list requires blank lengths, the gap and detailed matching dimensions.

A half-wave dipole is bent into a circle or square with a gap between its ends. A horizontal antenna is primarily horizontally polarized. Signal strength can vary with azimuth and installation. 3G‑Aerial cites 10–15 Ω as a reference range for the single-conductor Halo. The geometry calculator does not predict your antenna’s impedance.
Alexey (RA3POY) reported 69 Ω for his three-dimensional W2EEY/1 built for CB. The value describes that build.

The KK5JY diagram shows a shunt inductor across the feed terminals. Both loops share that feed in the original two-band design.
Top view of Halo. Gap g is opposite the feed point. D denotes diameter and S denotes side length.
The coax shield goes to the radiator. The centre conductor goes through capacitor C to the gamma rod, which connects back through the shorting strap.
Historical side view of the mounting arrangement. Two of the three supports are visible.
The shunt inductor L connects across the two feed contacts.
